dataset_family: Shenzhen University community-screening sample (212 community-dwelling elderly screened; 30 MCI and 30 demographically matched HC in the EEG experiment)
method_family: 64-channel task ERP (P2/P3) with ERP-microstate analysis during the Majority Function Task (cognitive load x surprise design), plus a neuropsychological battery
what_it_shows: In 30 MCI vs 30 demographically matched HC, task-evoked EEG differs by group mostly through group x load x surprise interactions (P2, P3, microstates C and D). Microstate B GFP gives a group main effect (MCI > HC, p < .01). RT on the same task does not separate the groups (p = .31), but accuracy does (97% vs 98%, p < .05). A load x group accuracy interaction exists: high load separates (94% vs 96%), low load does not (p = .14, near ceiling). Stroop time is the only neuropsychological test that does not separate (p = .10). No static measure that corresponds to the ERP is shown to fail while the ERP succeeds.
why: PDF identity confirmed: the map entry, DOI 10.1016/j.neuropsychologia.2021.108014, title and authors (He, Chen, Li, Hu, Wang, Wu, Yang, Guan; Shenzhen University) match the block, which lists only three of the eight authors. Read to the References. Electrophysiology limb: task-evoked EEG does differ between MCI and matched HC, but mostly as interactions. P2 and P3 show group x load x surprise interactions (F = 9.41, F = 9.17) with no group main effect, and microstates C and D show three-way interactions. The one group main effect is microstate B GFP (MCI > HC, F(1,58) = 7.82, p < .01), which the authors relate to the visual evoked potential, an early sensory component; the finder's reading did not mention it. The measure that fails alongside it is RT on the same task (group main effect p = .31), while accuracy on the same task did separate the groups (p < .05). A neural-versus-behavioural dissociation inside one loaded task is the P-661 pattern, which round 20 held is not a loaded-versus-static contrast (here there is at least a non-impaired comparator). The Stroop null (95.0 vs 83.3, p = .10) is not the corresponding static measure of any ERP, for three reasons: Stroop is itself an interference task; it was one of the executive tests used to classify MCI; and the paper never pairs it with the EEG results. Pairing it with the P3 would be a construct-level inference of the kind round 20 rejected for P-662 (HAMD vs LPP). Behavioural limb: accuracy on the Majority Function Task dissociates by load (high load separates, 94% vs 96%, p < .05; low load does not, p = .14; load x group F(1,58) = 4.51, p < .05). But the load is arrow congruency within one task, not a dual task, diffusion or ERP measure. Low-load accuracy sat at ceiling (99% overall), so its null says little. The overall accuracy group main effect was significant, so the task as a whole did separate the groups, and the effect is 2 percentage points. Verdict: partly, weak. The study shows the sensitivity half for task-evoked electrophysiology (the half P-666 was rated 'no' for showing alone), plus a behavioural load-by-group interaction outside the named families. It does not show a task-evoked electrophysiological measure separating MCI where the corresponding static measure fails. The authors note limited power from small numbers of subjects and trials (p.9). No verdict here depends on decoding mangled Elsevier glyphs. Independence: Shenzhen University community sample, with no overlap in site, cohort or authors with P-651, P-661, P-662, P-665/P-687 or P-666, or with P-522/P-1163. Note that the corpus holds a second paper from the same Guan lab and Shenzhen University group (P-433: Chen, He, Ding, Tao, Guan, Krueger), which may draw on the same community screening. It is neither a supporter nor a candidate here, but it matters if both are ever proposed. Method family: task ERP, which overlaps the task-ERP family of P-662 (a current supporter, rated 'no' in round 20). Not a preprint (Neuropsychologia 2021). supports_narrowed is n/a because the round-20 wording declares VF-25 not a convergence; the study does not supply the task-evoked electrophysiology dissociation that wording says no supporter shows.

quotes.quote: For half of the trials, all five arrows pointed in the same direction (5:0 condition, low cognitive load). For the other half of the trials, four arrows pointed in the same direction while one arrow pointed in the opposite direction (4:1 condition, high cognitive load).
evaluated executive function using the Trail Making Test Part B (TMT-B) (Gordon, 1972) and the Stroop Test (ST) (Koss et al., 2009)
Compared to the HC group, the MCI group showed significantly poorer performance on all the neuropsychological tests, except the Stroop Test (Table 1).
For accuracy, there was a significant main effect of group, F(1,58) = 5.12, p < .05
The MCI group showed significantly lower accuracy (M = 97%, SD = 2%) compared to the HC group (M = 98%, SD = 2%). The main effect of cognitive load was significant, F(1,58) = 109.18, p < .001

Accuracy was significantly higher for low cognitive load (M = 99%, SD = 1%) than for high cognitive load (M = 95%, SD = 4%). There was a significant two-way interaction between cognitive load and group, F(1,58) = 4.51, p < .05

Under the high load condition, the MCI group showed significantly lower accuracy (M = 94%, SD = 4%) than the HC group (M = 96%, SD = 4%, p < .05), while there was no significant group difference under the low load condition (p = .14).
For RT, the main effect of group was not significant, F(1,58) = 1.07, p = .31
The three-way interaction between group, cognitive load, and surprise level was significant, F(1,58) = 9.41, p < .01
The three-way interaction between group, cognitive load, and surprise level was significant, F(1,58) = 9.17, p < .01
For GFP, there was a significant main effect of group, F(1,58) = 7.82, p < .01
GFP was significantly smaller in the HC group (M = 1.81 μV, SD = 0.82 μV) than in the MCI group (M = 2.40 μV, SD = 0.82 μV).

In addition, the statistical power of this study was limited to some extent by small sizes of subjects and trials.
